newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats says EU not relevant to expansion.
newsitem.headline: Amplats says EU not relevant to expansion.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said on Tuesday the European Union's view of the South African platinum industry was not relevant to its planned restructuring or expansion.
The EU will decide on May 5 whether to grant regulatory approval of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's acquisition of 28.4 percent of Lonrho Plc.
The EU has said Anglo's stake in Lonrho effectively puts the platinum market under the control of Anglo and another South African mining house, Gencor Ltd.
But Amplats managing director Barry Davison, announcing a merger of the group's four platinum mines and a major mine expansion, said on Tuesday the EU stance had no bearing on the new moves.

"I don't believe the EU's attitude to the structure of the South African platinum industry has any bearing on those opportunities. I am sure that the EU is not in any position to decide by how much we should increase or decrease our production at any stage," he said.
"And certainly none of our plans are concerned with amalgamating, purchasing or merging with any existing producers.

"The opportunities I speak of are those in the market place for us to increase our production and so supply that increased demand which arises both from growth and demand and a reduction in Russian supplies. I don't believe the EU's positition is relevant to that or the merger of our operations," Davison said.

Amplats said earlier it planned to merge its four listed companies which at present constitute the group -- Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplat), Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd (Leplat), Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd (PP Rust) and Amplats itself.
The merger, together with the development of a new mine at Boschkoppie and expansion of PP Rust's concentrator, would enhance Amplats position as world leader in platinum, it said.
